messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: runtime-edge-prod p99 latency spike and increased 5xxs. p99 ~5.5s, errors ~7%. Alert link: https://grafana.redwood/runtime-edge-prod -> runtime-queue-high. Paging oncall.

Noah Green: oncall here, ack. tagging eng-runtime + eng-platform. grabbing initial flamegraphs and router traces.

Sofia Martinez: looking at request traces: a wave of large multi-step requests with heavy function calls and nested JSON outputs. KV cache hit rate down ~40% and connection queues at router are backlogged. A few tenants show repeated retriable bursts.

Ethan Brooks: immediate mitigations proposed: 1) apply ingress-level sliding window throttle for hosted tier (60s window), 2) reduce runtime max_in_flight per-worker from 48 -> 12, 3) enable queue_shedding: queued requests beyond 1.5s return 429 w/ Retry-After, 4) temporarily disable experimental-features flag that enables long_function_output. Also consider lowering per-request deadline to 3s.

Ravi Patel: agree with plan. I'll execute the gateway throttle and feature flag flip. Noah, can you make the runtime override canary?

Noah Green: creating canary payload (5%):

```
# runtime canary
POST https://admin.internal/runtime/config
Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN
{
  "service":"runtime-edge-prod",
  "canary":5,
  "overrides":{
    "max_in_flight":12,
    "request_deadline_ms":3000,
    "queue_shedding_ms":1500,
    "shed_response_code":429
  }
}
```

deploy-bot: rollout started rtf-20240702-1749 -> runtime-edge-prod canary 5%.

Ravi Patel: applying gateway sliding-window throttle for hosted tier:

```
PUT https://gateway.internal/admin/tiers/hosted/throttle
{
  "window_secs":60,
  "max_requests":1200,
  "burst":200,
  "reason":"mitigation - reduce noisy bursts"
}
```

Ravi Patel: toggling feature flag experimental-long-output -> OFF for hosted.

CS-bot: Notifying CS team: potential impact to hosted devs and a handful of paid customers if we enforce hard sheds. Template in #customer-notify-drafts.

Sofia Martinez: canary metrics: canary pods p99 dropped from 5.5s -> 1.9s, 5xxs down to ~2.4%. We are seeing shed 429s on canary ~0.9% as expected. KV cache churn reduced.

Ethan Brooks: good. ramping canary to 25% after 6m stable. also enabling short-term per-tenant bypass list for known paid customers (acct-ny-1, acct-la-3) to avoid breaking SLAs. Noah, please make the bypass list editable by CS with audit log.

Noah Green: adding bypass list and making it editable via infra-admin role.

deploy-bot: rollout progressing 5% -> 25% -> 65%. id rtf-20240702-1749.

Sofia Martinez: at 65% rollout p99 ~1.1s. overall error rate down to 1.4%. queuedepth across pods normalized. Gateway telemetry shows inbound rate reduced ~33%.

Ravi Patel: note: we disabled experimental-long-output which will change responses shape for some hosted devs. CS-bot, please prepare a dev bulletin and include how to re-enable for dedicated/custom tenants.

CS-bot: drafting notice for hosted devs, will post to status and email affected AEs for paid tenants.

Ethan Brooks: follow-up: one internal customer-run batch job still causing repeated long flows; it's on tenant acct-intg-5. consider contacting owner and asking to reschedule or run in dedicated env.

Noah Green: full rollout to 100% after 10m stable window. applying final config.

deploy-bot: rollout complete rtf-20240702-1749 -> 100%.

Sofia Martinez: post-rollout metrics: p99 ~0.8s, 5xxs ~0.8%. Shedding at ~1.5% globally. Some hosted devs reported 429s and different output format; CS notified. Router queue_depth stable.

Ravi Patel: immediate mitigation successful. Handoff to Priya for monitoring. Priya offline? Priya out, I'll hand to Noah for next 90m.

Noah Green: taking handoff until 10:30 UTC. Key watch: p99 >2s or shed >5% or any paid tenant reporting degraded SLA.

Ethan Brooks: action items and long-term fixes to capture in incident doc:
- eng-runtime: implement adaptive concurrency per-route based on observed cost heuristics (per-model, per-route max_in_flight).
- eng-platform: implement per-tenant dynamic sliding-window throttles and an emergency tenant-override workflow for CS.
- eng-ml: add early-cost-prediction in frontend to reject/trim obviously expensive requests (multi-tool, massive function output) before hitting runtime.
- infra: bake a quick cache-clear playbook and tooling for stuck KV shards discovered in traces.
- cs: contact affected tenants, gather exact request IDs and sample payloads for debugging.

CS-bot: CS has sent targeted messages to affected paid accounts and posted a status update to status.redwood.ai. Estimated affected: ~200 hosted dev tokens, 3 paid accounts with transient errors.

Noah Green: logging incident INC-2024-07-02-edge-backpressure. Marking mitigated but keeping channel open for postmortem notes. Please attach config diff blob and a short timeline in the incident doc.

Sofia Martinez: hypothesis: a small fraction of extremely expensive request patterns (bulk ops + long outputs) starved worker slots which caused queue growth and KV cache eviction. Disabling the long-output feature and reducing max_in_flight shed excess load and recovered latency. Long-term we need predictive culling and tenant-aware quotas.

Ravi Patel: thanks team. reopening pager if SLA hits. handing off monitoring to Noah. :white_check_mark:

Noah Green: acknowledged. monitoring for 90m and will start the postmortem doc after 60m if stable. Thanks all.
